title: Namespaces, dependency declarations and package boundaries
outcome: Use exported namespace-qualified functions and inspect a local package source layout without confusing sourced definitions with an installed package.
mechanism:
A package namespace separates names that belong to one package from names in the current workspace. stats::median selects an exported function even when another function called median is present in the global environment. library attaches exported names to the search path for convenience; it does not make every unqualified name immune to masking. Namespace qualification is useful when the originating dependency is part of the analytical contract.

The double-colon operator accesses exported objects. Triple-colon access reaches implementation details that the package author has not offered as a stable public interface. A function being reachable is not a reason to depend on it. getNamespaceExports and getExportedValue provide inspectable public interfaces without guessing internal names. Use the exact prepared package and record versions when behavior matters.

A minimal package source tree has DESCRIPTION metadata, a NAMESPACE declaration and R source files beneath R/. DESCRIPTION lists dependencies, while NAMESPACE controls exports and method registrations. Listing a package in Imports records a dependency; it does not by itself attach that package or make every function available without qualification. Names prefixed with a dot are conventional internal names, not access-control guarantees.

The worked tree exports observed_mean while keeping its helper out of NAMESPACE. The script writes only to its own temporary directory, parses the source and evaluates its own authored definitions in a new environment. This is a local source-layout demonstration. It does not install a package, create an actual package namespace, test lazy loading or run R CMD check. The cleanup handler deletes that temporary tree when the demonstration returns.

For a real reusable package, continue in a separately prepared multi-file contributor workspace: maintain DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE, document public functions, add tests, build and install locally, then run R CMD check. Those steps need their own file/project workflow. The classroom pad runs one main.R and does not turn a temporary demonstration directory into a permanent downloadable package.

Choose dependencies because they supply a needed public behavior. A small mean function uses base code; a statistical density can call stats::dnorm explicitly. Avoid installing packages inside analytical lesson code. The classroom dependencies are prepared separately, and source execution remains offline. Tests should establish numerical outputs, dependency resolution and public-interface boundaries without treating a package scaffold as installation evidence.

vocabulary.definition: A package-specific environment and name-resolution boundary.
A name the package exposes through its public interface.
A DESCRIPTION dependency field, distinct from attaching a package to the search path.
The package file declaring exports, imports and method registrations.

anatomy: stats::median resolves an exported name regardless of a global median binding. getExportedValue("stats","median") retrieves that public function. read.dcf reads DESCRIPTION metadata; parse validates R syntax. sys.source here evaluates only the script's own local definitions in a chosen environment and does not emulate package installation.

worked_examples.title: Qualification survives a masked name
worked_examples.code:
median <- function(x, ...) -999
x <- c(1, 4, 9)
stopifnot(median(x) == -999, stats::median(x) == 4)
public <- getExportedValue("stats", "median")
stopifnot(public(x) == 4, "median" %in% getNamespaceExports("stats"))
print(c(masked = median(x), qualified = stats::median(x)))
worked_examples.explanation: The deliberately masked global name shows why dependency-qualified calls carry useful information. The exported function remains available through the namespace without depending on the search-path ordering.

worked_examples.title: Inspect a bounded package-shaped source tree
worked_examples.code:
inspect_local_package <- function() {
  root <- tempfile("measurekit-")
  dir.create(root)
  on.exit(unlink(root, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  dir.create(file.path(root, "R"))
  writeLines(c(
    "Package: measurekit", "Version: 0.0.1", "Title: Local Contract Example",
    "Description: Demonstrates a bounded package source layout.",
    "License: MIT", "Authors@R: person('Example', 'Author', role=c('aut','cre'), email='example@example.invalid')",
    "Imports: stats"
  ), file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION"))
  writeLines("export(observed_mean)", file.path(root, "NAMESPACE"))
  definition <- c(
    ".validate <- function(x) {",
    "  if (!is.numeric(x) || any(!is.finite(x))) stop('finite numeric values required')",
    "  x", "}",
    "observed_mean <- function(x) {",
    "  x <- .validate(x)",
    "  if (!length(x)) return(NA_real_)",
    "  mean(x)", "}"
  )
  writeLines(definition, file.path(root, "R", "summary.R"))
  metadata <- read.dcf(file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION"))
  stopifnot(metadata[1, "Package"] == "measurekit")
  stopifnot(identical(readLines(file.path(root, "NAMESPACE")), "export(observed_mean)"))
  parsed <- parse(file.path(root, "R", "summary.R"), keep.source = FALSE)
  stopifnot(length(parsed) == 2L)
  environment <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
  sys.source(file.path(root, "R", "summary.R"), envir = environment)
  stopifnot(environment$observed_mean(c(2, 4)) == 3)
  list(files = sort(list.files(root, recursive = TRUE)), mean = environment$observed_mean(c(2, 4)))
}

result <- inspect_local_package()
stopifnot(identical(result$files, c("DESCRIPTION", "NAMESPACE", "R/summary.R")), result$mean == 3)
print(result)
worked_examples.explanation: The temporary files demonstrate metadata, exports and source placement. Evaluating the known definitions proves their local behavior, while the guide explicitly separates that from installation and package-check evidence.
worked_examples.expected: Three expected source files and mean 3; the temporary directory is removed.

exercises.prompt: Predict the difference between a global median and stats::median.
exercises.hint: Resolve the qualified call through the package export.
exercises.answer: The masked function can return -999 while stats::median(c(1,4,9)) remains 4.

exercises.prompt: Retrieve the public median function without attaching stats names.
exercises.hint: Use getExportedValue with explicit package and name.

exercises.prompt: Create and inspect DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE and one R source file in a temporary tree.
exercises.hint: Keep all paths below the owned temporary directory.
exercises.answer: The source tree contains package metadata, export(observed_mean), and R/summary.R. Parse and evaluate only the known authored definitions.
exercises.expected: Exact three-file inventory and checked local behavior.

exercises.prompt: Diagnose a helper being considered private merely because its name starts with a dot.
exercises.hint: Naming convention is not the namespace export policy.
exercises.answer: The NAMESPACE export list controls ordinary public access. A dot name alone neither registers nor hides an export.
exercises.expected: Separate naming convention and public interface.

exercises.prompt: Test empty and nonfinite values in the local observed_mean function.
exercises.hint: The public contract permits an empty set but rejects an infinite measurement.
exercises.answer: Empty input returnsNA_real_; nonfinite input raises the finite-values error.

exercises.prompt: Describe what remains before claiming that the temporary tree is an installed, checked package.
exercises.hint: Parsing and sys.source do not perform package installation.
exercises.answer: Use a separate multi-file project to document, build, install and run R CMD check. Preserve tests and dependency declarations; do not run network installation from this pad.

assert_error <- function(expr, pattern) {
  message <- tryCatch(
    {
      force(expr); NULL
    },
    error = conditionMessage
  )
  stopifnot(is.character(message), length(message) == 1L, grepl(pattern, message))
}

stopifnot(median(c(1, 4, 9)) == -999, stats::median(c(1, 4, 9)) == 4)
public <- getExportedValue("stats", "median")
stopifnot(public(c(1, 4, 9)) == 4, "median" %in% getNamespaceExports("stats"))
result <- inspect_local_package()
stopifnot(identical(result$files, c("DESCRIPTION", "NAMESPACE", "R/summary.R")), result$mean == 3)
observed_mean <- function(x) {
  if (!is.numeric(x) || any(!is.finite(x))) stop("finite numeric values required")
  if (!length(x)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(x)
}
stopifnot(is.na(observed_mean(numeric(0))))
assert_error(observed_mean(c(1, Inf)), "finite numeric values")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(stats::dnorm(0), 1 / sqrt(2 * pi))))
cat("r-026 reference checks passed\n")
solution_explanation:
The reference demonstrates search-path masking and then deliberately resolves the public package export. It checks the exact source-tree inventory and the behavior of the authored function in a separate environment.

The tree is removed after inspection, and no installation or network call occurs. A local source environment is not a package namespace. Empty-input and invalid-value tests belong to the function's contract and would be retained in a real package test suite during the optional multi-file continuation.
